pharm: Irreversibly inhibits the gastric H+/K+ ATPase (proton pump) in parietal cells, suppressing basal and stimulated gastric acid secretion.
quick: Take before eating in the morning
Generally considered low risk; use if needed
Present in milk; limited data; likely compatible
summary: Omeprazole is a proton pump inhibitor. The OTC product is indicated for frequent heartburn (occurring 2 or more days a week) as a 14-day course. It is not intended for immediate relief and may take 1 to 4 days for full effect.
indications: Treatment of frequent heartburn (occurring 2 or more days a week)
Note: OTC product is not intended for immediate heartburn relief

dosage.d: 1 tablet (20 mg) once daily before eating in the morning
dosage.t: 14 days; may repeat a 14-day course every 4 months
dosage.n: Do not take more than 1 tablet a day; swallow whole
Heartburn in children may indicate a serious condition

admin: Swallow one tablet whole with a glass of water before eating in the morning
Do not chew or crush tablets
Do not take more than 1 tablet a day
Do not use for more than 14 days or more often than every 4 months unless directed by a doctor
moa: Omeprazole is a substituted-benzimidazole PPI activated in the acidic parietal cell canaliculus, where it covalently and irreversibly inhibits the H+/K+ ATPase, the terminal step of gastric acid secretion. Restoration of acid output requires synthesis of new enzyme.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to omeprazole, substituted benzimidazoles, or formulation components
relative: Long-term high-dose therapy (fracture, hypomagnesemia, B12 deficiency risks)
Drugs requiring gastric acidity for absorption

preg: No evidence of major risk from available human data; generally considered acceptable when indicated. Use if clearly needed.
lact: Omeprazole is present in human milk; limited data suggest low infant exposure. Considered likely compatible; weigh maternal need.
renal: No dosage adjustment required in renal impairment.
hepatic: Bioavailability and AUC increase in hepatic impairment due to reduced clearance; consider dose reduction.

major: Clopidogrel (omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, reducing active metabolite; avoid combination)
pH-dependent drugs (atazanavir, nelfinavir, ketoconazole, itraconazole, erlotinib - reduced absorption)
moderate: Diazepam, phenytoin, cilostazol (increased levels via CYP2C19)
interactions.food: Take before eating in the morning.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive secretin stimulation test; affects CgA levels.

monitoring: Reassess continued need; seek care if heartburn persists after 14-day course
counsel: May take 1 to 4 days for full effect; not for immediate relief
Do not exceed 1 tablet daily or use beyond 14 days without a doctor
See a doctor if heartburn continues, or if you have trouble swallowing, chest/shoulder pain, or vomiting blood
Tell your clinician if you take clopidogrel
pk: Acid suppression within hours; full effect 1-4 days
Up to 72 hours of acid suppression
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from light and moisture
pearls: OTC dose is for frequent heartburn 2+ days/week, not immediate relief
Strong CYP2C19 inhibitor - avoid with clopidogrel
Effect outlasts plasma half-life due to irreversible pump binding
Limit to 14-day courses every 4 months unless directed by a clinician
missed: If a daily dose is missed, take it when remembered the same day; if near the next day's dose, skip it. Do not take more than one tablet per day.
overdose: No specific antidote; omeprazole is extensively protein-bound and not readily dialyzable. Manage symptomatically and supportively.
